categories.name: Direct Payment
categories.description: Cases that result in a prompt payment either immediately after fine creation or shortly after sending the fine, with short trace lengths and durations.
categories.rationale: High frequency variants like V0002 and V0007 show a straightforward path from fine creation to payment without complex notifications or appeals.

categories.name: Standard Fine Lifecycle with Penalties
categories.description: Standard progression involving fine notification, addition of penalties, and standard closure paths like credit collection or delayed payment.
categories.rationale: Represents the most common heavy traffic patterns (e.g., V0001, V0004) where notifications and penalties are standard steps leading to either eventual payment or credit collection.

categories.name: Payment Rework Loops
categories.description: Cases characterized by a high frequency of repeated payment activities stretching trace lengths and durations significantly.
categories.rationale: Variants such as V0005, V0006, and V0153 demonstrate multiple repeated payment actions indicating installment-like behavior or processing corrections.

categories.name: Appeal and Legal Proceedings
categories.description: Complex variants involving appeals to the prefecture or judge, results processing, and extended durations spanning several years.
categories.rationale: Variants like V0008, V0057, and V0103 involve formal appeal steps, long waiting times, and interactions with external legal authorities.
